# Review protocol reference

Defaults are the values of the original review; `changed` marks project overrides.

## identification

Benchmark coverage: do the seed papers come back from each database export?

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jw_benchmark` | `0.88` | `0.88` | Jaro-Winkler title similarity above which an export record counts as a candidate match for a benchmark paper (after DOI and exact normalised title). Candidates below the confirm threshold are flagged for a look. |
| `jw_confirm` | `0.95` | `0.95` | Minimum title similarity for joining imported labels or decisions to the corpus by title. Coverage flags every fuzzy benchmark match for a look, whatever its similarity. |
| `validation_after_freeze` | `true` | `true` | Report the validation benchmark set only after the query is frozen (develop on one set, test once on the other). |
| `development_share` | `0.57` | `0.57` | Share of the seed (benchmark) papers the suggested random split assigns to the development set (the original review used 12 of 21); the rest form the validation set, which is tested once. |
| `record_budget` | `5000` | `5000` | Records the team can screen from the accepted query. Over it, the suggested edits that save records without losing a development seed are listed first; the diagnosis says how far over it is. |
## imports

Export sanity checks at import: is each file plausibly the result of the query, and is it complete?

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_benchmark_hits` | `1` | `1` | A file that contains fewer benchmark papers than this (DOI, exact title or fuzzy title at identification.jw_benchmark) fails the benchmark signal of the off-topic check. |
| `min_vocabulary_overlap` | `0.5` | `0.5` | Minimum share of records whose title or abstract contains at least one term of the synonyms artifact (approved or frozen version; a draft is used with a note when none is approved). Below this the file fails the vocabulary signal. A file is 'off_topic' only when every available signal fails. |
| `warn_on_export_cap` | `true` | `true` | Flag a file whose record count equals the platform's known export cap for that format (platforms.yaml export_cap): the export was probably truncated to one batch. |
## dedup

Deduplication stages A (DOI), B (exact normalised title), C (fuzzy title with corroboration).

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jw_candidate` | `0.85` | `0.85` | Minimum fuzzy title similarity for a pair to enter stage C at all. |
| `jw_auto_merge` | `0.97` | `0.97` | Similarity above which a pair with a full citation match is merged automatically. |
| `jw_corroborated` | `0.9` | `0.9` | Similarity above which a pair is merged when the year and the first author or journal agree, at least two locators (volume, issue, first page, article number) match and neither the DOIs nor the publication types conflict. |
| `jw_strong_title` | `0.95` | `0.95` | Merges nothing by itself: pairs with the same first author and year at or above it are put near the top of the manual queue, and pairs with different DOIs and different first authors below it are ruled not duplicates. |
| `doi_conflict_title` | `0.7` | `0.7` | Pairs sharing a DOI but with title similarity below this (or years more than two apart) go to the manual queue as DOI conflicts, unless a full citation match confirms them. |
| `generic_title_max_words` | `4` | `4` | Short titles (Introduction, Erratum): when the first record of a pair has at most this many title words, an exact-title merge on two locators also needs the first author or journal to match. No rule merges on title alone, at any length. |
## corpus

What counts as a usable abstract and how much text is embedded.

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thin_words` | `20` | `20` | An abstract with fewer words is 'thin': it is enriched, excluded from the embedding of its own text, sampled as a separate pool and never leads to an 'absent' grade in screening. |
| `max_words` | `3000` | `3000` | Title + abstract + keywords are cut at this many words before embedding. |
## enrichment

Where missing abstracts are fetched from, in order; a found abstract is never overwritten.

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sources` | `["openalex", "crossref", "europepmc", "semantic_scholar"]` | `["openalex", "crossref", "europepmc", "semantic_scholar"]` | Metadata services tried in this order for each thin record with a DOI. |
| `title_search_min_jw` | `0.95` | `0.95` | Records without a DOI are looked up by title; a hit must reach this title similarity and the year within one. |
## ranking

Anchor ranking: cosine between each record and one aims-only anchor per cell; sorts, never filters.

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `top_n_cells` | `2` | `2` | A record's score is the mean of its N highest cell similarities (the review used 2; 1 and 3 are compared). |
| `top_n_compare` | `[1, 2, 3]` | `[1, 2, 3]` | Alternative N values reported in the validation table. |
| `recall_at` | `[100, 250, 1000, 3000]` | `[100, 250, 1000, 3000]` | Ranks K at which benchmark recall is reported. |
| `cluster_top` | `3000` | `3000` | Depth of the ranking that is clustered and shown in the explorer; also the deepest band that is cluster-balanced. |
| `cluster_k` | `8` | `8` | Number of k-means clusters (topics) in the top of the ranking. |
| `cluster_terms` | `8` | `8` | Distinctive terms listed per cluster. |
| `recall_at_pct` | `[1.0, 5.0, 10.0, 25.0, 50.0]` | `[1.0, 5.0, 10.0, 25.0, 50.0]` | Percentiles p of the ranking at which benchmark recall is also reported: a paper counts when its rank is at most floor(p/100 x ranked records). |
## sampling

Human labelling samples: a band-stratified probability sample (recall estimate) and a purposive development set.

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bands` | `[{"name": "S1", "start": 1, "end": 100, "n": null, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S2", "start": 101, "end": 300, "n": 70, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S3", "start": 301, "end": 1000, "n": 60, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S4", "start": 1001, "end": 3000, "n": 46, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S5", "start": 3001, "end": null, "n": 40, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}]` | `[{"name": "S1", "start": 1, "end": 100, "n": null, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S2", "start": 101, "end": 300, "n": 70, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S3", "start": 301, "end": 1000, "n": 60, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S4", "start": 1001, "end": 3000, "n": 46, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}, {"name": "S5", "start": 3001, "end": null, "n": 40, "start_pct": null, "end_pct": null}]` | Rank bands of the probability sample with the number drawn per band (None = census). The recall estimate weights each band by N_h/n_h. |
| `probability_sample` | `"validation"` | `"validation"` | Name of the probability sample. |
| `development_sample` | `"development"` | `"development"` | Name of the purposive development sample. |
| `development_reviewers` | `1` | `1` | Reviewers for the development sample: one, or two (agreement or adjudication needed). With one, a record is complete with one final label; with two, at least two reviewers labelled it and all agree, or it is adjudicated. Applies to every purposive sample; until every record is complete, screening runs that include its records are refused and earlier model output on them is hidden. |
| `per_cell` | `4` | `4` | Likely includes drawn per construct cell from its top-scoring records. |
| `per_near_miss` | `4` | `4` | Records drawn per near-miss description (adjacent literatures have their own count, per_adjacent). |
| `near_miss_pool` | `12` | `12` | Highest-ranked records considered per near-miss description. |
| `near_miss_max_rank` | `3000` | `3000` | Near-miss candidates must rank within this depth. |
| `per_adjacent` | `4` | `4` | Marginal cases drawn per approved adjacent literature: the records within near_miss_max_rank closest to the literature's description and example phrases. Draws nothing while no literature is approved, so the development set is unchanged unless the researcher names adjacent literatures. |
| `per_cluster` | `2` | `2` | Records per cluster for topical coverage (medoid first). |
| `per_boundary` | `4` | `4` | Boundary cases drawn per near-miss entry and per approved adjacent literature, after every other pool: at random from the near_miss_pool records within near_miss_max_rank that score highest on both the best cell and that entry (the lower of the two rank percentiles). No model call. |
| `n_thin` | `5` | `5` | Thin-abstract records in the development set. |
| `n_tail` | `3` | `3` | Clearly irrelevant records drawn from beyond the cluster depth. |
| `pool_size` | `100` | `100` | Top candidates per cell considered when drawing likely includes. |
| `min_per_band` | `10` | `10` | Fewest records the validation planner gives a sampled band (never more than the band holds). |
| `plan_sims` | `400` | `400` | Simulated samples per allocation in the validation planner (seeded; at most 2000). |
| `plan_seconds` | `30` | `30` | Time limit of one validation plan in seconds; past it the table is marked approximate. |
| `plan_power` | `0.8` | `0.8` | Chance of a clear answer (target met or not met) the planner and the suggestion ask for when they search for the number of labels. |
## screening

LLM screening calls and the corpus protocol built on them.

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote_min_chars` | `8` | `8` | The shortest verbatim fragment that counts as a found quote. The model quotes the words behind every grade; an absent grade whose quote has no fragment this long in the title or abstract becomes unclear (recall first). |
| `max_tokens` | `2000` | `2000` | Output token budget of one screening call. |
| `passes` | `2` | `2` | Independent reads of every record before the tie-break. With 1, pass A alone decides: no pass B, no third read, and the majority is not used. |
| `blind_third_read` | `true` | `true` | Where the two reads disagree, a third read with its own seed decides. |
| `majority` | `2` | `2` | Votes needed for a decision; a three-way split becomes 'maybe'. |
| `second_screen` | `true` | `true` | Re-read every 'maybe' twice (plus tie-break) in a second protocol. Off: `wider screen second` and the UI job are refused. |
| `recall_first` | `true` | `true` | Rule: 'absent' without a verified quote becomes 'unclear'; exclude only when unrelated or verifiably absent. Off: the model's grades and exclusions stand (maybe flags and unverified-quote flags still apply). |
| `maybe_flags` | `[]` | `[]` | Boolean fields of the screening schema that force 'maybe' when true (e.g. a contamination flag). |
## recall

Stratified recall estimate on the probability sample against human labels.

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `primary_variant` | `"lenient"` | `"lenient"` | strict = includes kept as include; lenient = includes kept as include or maybe; cautious = includes and maybes kept as include or maybe. |
| `bootstrap_b` | `10000` | `10000` | Bootstrap replicates for the cross-check interval in the technical report (stratified, seeded; census strata fixed); at most 50,000 are run, a larger value is capped with a note. The primary interval is the approximate design-based interval on the effective number of relevant papers (report section "Recall: method"). |
| `ci_level` | `0.95` | `0.95` | Confidence level of the intervals. |
| `target` | `null` | `null` | Recall the screening should reach, judged on exact bounds valid at every look; set it before any recall result is seen (wider validation target). Empty = no target. |
| `low_recall_rule` | `null` | `null` | What you will do when the target is not met: count maybes as kept, screen the top strata by hand, or revise the prompt and validate on a fresh sample. |
| `top_strata_depth` | `null` | `null` | Depth of the ranking screened by hand under the top-strata rule. |
| `precision` | `null` | `null` | Planned margin: the estimate minus the exact lower bound should not exceed it. Empty = none (no default). |
| `suggest_seconds` | `20` | `20` | Time limit of the suggestion of how many more labels may be needed; past it the suggestion is approximate. |
| `practical_labels` | `500` | `500` | How many more labels you consider practical for validation. When settling whether the recall target is met is expected to need more, WIDER warns that it may be impractical; the warning never blocks anything, and you may stop and report the result as inconclusive. |
## labelling

Extra categorical labels the screening LLM assigns per record (beyond the fixed decision vocabulary).

| key | value | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | `[]` | `[]` | Project-specific labels, e.g. the actor type, the setting, or an adjacent literature. Each becomes a field of the screening schema, a column of the decisions export and a breakdown in the recall report. |
